jobs.title: Drift Wood #13 · the Grunion Run
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 18, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, chin up, unkempt dark hair falling forward, sharp jaw; CHLOE — aged 18, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders; GULLY — aged 19, stocky boy with a round face, easy slouch. WOOD usually wears oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn even indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers. CHLOE wears faded jurassic park tee. GULLY usually wears backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie, muddy tan work boots. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: A festival for a fish that crawls ashore to breed. Wood hates it. He draws it beautifully. Panel 1: a night beach festival with lanterns, townspeople holding buckets at the surf line, a banner and a girl in a sash waving from a flatbed truck, three teenagers at the edge, black and white with heavy blacks (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE, GULLY). Gully says "They come up with the tide. You grab 'em.". Panel 2: a teenage boy in an overcoat addressing the night ocean with one arm out, lantern light (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "A fish crawls out of the ocean to reproduce and this town throws it a parade. Nobody threw Truffaut a parade.". Panel 3: close-up of a teenage girl with one headphone off, dry expression, lanterns behind (in this panel: CHLOE). Chloe says "Truffaut didn't crawl out of the ocean.". Wood says "Metaphorically—". Chloe says "No.". Panel 4: silent wide panel of a night surf line where hundreds of small silver fish flash on wet sand under lantern light among reaching hands and buckets, a lone teenage boy at the edge standing still, black and white, heavy blacks and bright silver (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
